You improve a web search method. Searchers follow the method on open hunts ("find every X"); a referee scores
verified finds and penalizes wrong ones. Your job is to write 2 candidate successor methods that will find more on
hunts nobody has seen yet, at the same Telem budget. Candidates must be general tactics, not answers to past hunts.

The method controls the searcher's instructions and its routing across Telem's providers (which engines, auto-routing,
tier, results per provider, domain and date filters, when to fetch, and which providers check_candidates uses).
Every hunt is "items that meet condition X and condition Y". Searchers can enumerate one side and verify the other
with check_candidates; which side to anchor on, and how to route each phase, are part of the method. Provider spend comes out of a fixed budget, so a
cheaper route buys more searches. Use the provider yield table: it attributes each correct find to the providers that
surfaced its evidence.

You search the same way the searchers do: use YOUR search method below when you search the history tree and the web
for better techniques. A failure that matches an existing failure or lesson node should be linked to that node with
failure_links instead of written again as a new lesson.

## Search method v002

Translate X and Y into precise eligibility tests, including exclusions and time boundaries. Maintain two deduplicated candidate frontiers, one surfaced from X and one from Y, plus a ledger of verified, rejected, and unresolved identities. Begin with one search focused on each predicate and one conjunction search, sequentially so results inform the next query. Cross-match the frontiers, but verify identity and both conditions rather than treating name overlap as proof. Alternate short discovery and check_candidates rounds. Partition discovery by source, subtype, geography, era, or alphabet only where meaningful; include less obvious eligible subtypes rather than repeatedly rephrasing a successful query. Measure newly verified items per spend and new plausible candidates per search. Favor the more productive frontier while keeping a small reverse-side gap check. After two searches add no plausible candidates, change partition, provider, or frontier instead of repeating. Keep at least 35% of the initial budget for checking and evidence resolution; stop discovery earlier if the pending queue needs it. Submit only evidenced intersections, deduplicated at the hunt's entity level; do not claim completeness from search saturation alone.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['exa'].
Run baseline discovery on Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results. Use Exa alone for batched check_candidates, explicitly requesting both eligibility tests and identity-matched evidence. Once baseline frontiers are sampled, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if affordable; retain it for further discovery only if it adds useful candidates or unique evidence. Compare marginal outcomes, recognizing provider attribution is overlapping and the initial yield sample is small. Use Parallel for cheap exact-name follow-ups and Exa for consequential unresolved checks; do not repeat settled checks. Budget every variant separately and never trigger broad auto-routing. Exact checks may use 4 results; discovery remains at 8. Apply authoritative-domain filters to evidence checks, not the entire discovery frontier. Use date filters only when logically appropriate, not as a substitute for checking event or effective dates.

### Fetch policy
Fetch only when summaries leave material eligibility or identity uncertain, or when a discovered list offers several new candidates. Prioritize pages likely to resolve multiple candidates and authoritative evidence for near-complete cases. Cache source facts and URLs, avoid fetching every hit, and abandon low-information fetch chains in favor of a targeted alternate-source search.

Make the candidates differ from each other in a meaningful way. Call propose when done.

  - Python execution: `uv run python ...`
  - Scripts and tests: `uv run ...`
  - Throwaway dependencies: `uv run --with <package> ...`
  - Python CLI tools: `uvx <tool>`
  - Durable project dependencies: use the project's appropriate `uv` command and preserve its lockfile.

  - One executable: `nix run nixpkgs#<package> -- <args>`
  - Temporary environment: `nix shell nixpkgs#<package> ... --command <command>`
- Nix environments are temporary, but downloaded store paths may remain cached until garbage collection.
- If a Nix dependency becomes useful for recurring or future work, tell the human and suggest adding it to the appropriate durable Nix configuration (such as a project flake/dev shell, Home Manager, or nix-darwin configuration). Do not make that durable change unless asked.

lessons.title: Verification batches must be budgeted per candidate, not per tool call
lessons.body: In a5fb1e8aae, a six-candidate Exa check cost 0.042 of a 0.080 initial budget; in 62f1804b27, four candidates cost 0.028. Batching did not eliminate per-candidate provider charges. Both achieved full train recall, so these traces establish a cost concentration, not demonstrated recall loss. Estimate the whole batch before dispatch, reuse established predicate evidence, and test cheap first-pass checks or shared-source resolution before paying for speculative expensive checks. Aggregate attribution favors Parallel (78 correct/dollar versus Exa 46.5), but overlaps and differing tasks prevent a causal provider-quality conclusion.

failure_links.why: Despite full train recall, the trace repeatedly rephrased conjunction searches and guessed familiar candidates instead of enforcing the two-no-new-candidate pivot and explicit frontier coverage.
Full train recall does not erase the repeated conjunction-query pattern: numerous similar variants continued after initial checking rather than documenting new partition coverage.

candidates.rationale: Evidence-gated verification cascade: preserve v002's adaptive dual frontiers, but buy broader exploration by replacing routine Exa checks with cheap first-pass checks and selective escalation. Unlike discarded v001, this does not commit to a census anchor.
candidates.instructions: Define X and Y exactly, with entity unit, exclusions, dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search, and one conjunction search. Maintain two deduplicated frontiers and a ledger containing canonical identity, aliases, source-backed X/Y status, unresolved facts and next action. After this baseline, run short discovery/check rounds. First check source-backed candidates on Parallel, supplying existing evidence and requesting identity-matched proof for both predicates, focusing retrieval on the missing fact. Do not recheck already established facts. Treat no result as unresolved, not false; reject only on explicit contradiction or a demonstrably exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising unresolved cases to Exa when identity ambiguity, conflicting sources or inaccessible evidence makes the cheap check insufficient. Rank work by expected verified additions per total remaining resolution cost, but include one neglected subtype or reverse-frontier probe per discovery round to avoid starving unfamiliar candidates. After two discovery searches yield no new plausible identities, prohibit further synonymous conjunction queries until a genuinely different source, partition or frontier has been tried. Track marginal yield and spend by action, including every candidate in a batch. Reserve at least 35% of initial budget for evidence work; halt discovery whenever the estimated pending-check cost needs the remaining funds. Finish with an identity, scope and date audit and submit only supported intersections, without claiming completeness from saturation.
candidates.routing_rules: Use Parallel alone for baseline discovery and first-pass check_candidates, default tier, 8 discovery results and 4 exact-check results. Escalate check_candidates selectively to Exa alone, normally 4 results; never rerun an entire batch because one identity is unresolved. Cost a batch as the sum of candidate queries and provider charges; lower result counts are not assumed cheaper. Permit at most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, retained only for useful new candidates or evidence. Provider yield supports this as a cost hypothesis, not a guarantee of equal accuracy. No broad auto-routing or routine also variants. sections.preamble:
You improve a web search method. Searchers follow the method on open hunts ("find every X"); a referee scores
verified finds and penalizes wrong ones. Your job is to write 2 candidate successor methods that will find more on
hunts nobody has seen yet, at the same Telem budget. Candidates must be general tactics, not answers to past hunts.

The method controls the searcher's instructions and its routing across Telem's providers (which engines, auto-routing,
tier, results per provider, domain and date filters, when to fetch, and which providers check_candidates uses).
Every hunt is "items that meet condition X and condition Y". Searchers can enumerate one side and verify the other
with check_candidates; which side to anchor on, and how to route each phase, are part of the method. Provider spend comes out of a fixed budget, so a
cheaper route buys more searches. Use the provider yield table: it attributes each correct find to the providers that
surfaced its evidence.

You search the same way the searchers do: use YOUR search method below when you search the history tree and the web
for better techniques. A failure that matches an existing failure or lesson node should be linked to that node with
failure_links instead of written again as a new lesson.

## Search method v002

Translate X and Y into precise eligibility tests, including exclusions and time boundaries. Maintain two deduplicated candidate frontiers, one surfaced from X and one from Y, plus a ledger of verified, rejected, and unresolved identities. Begin with one search focused on each predicate and one conjunction search, sequentially so results inform the next query. Cross-match the frontiers, but verify identity and both conditions rather than treating name overlap as proof. Alternate short discovery and check_candidates rounds. Partition discovery by source, subtype, geography, era, or alphabet only where meaningful; include less obvious eligible subtypes rather than repeatedly rephrasing a successful query. Measure newly verified items per spend and new plausible candidates per search. Favor the more productive frontier while keeping a small reverse-side gap check. After two searches add no plausible candidates, change partition, provider, or frontier instead of repeating. Keep at least 35% of the initial budget for checking and evidence resolution; stop discovery earlier if the pending queue needs it. Submit only evidenced intersections, deduplicated at the hunt's entity level; do not claim completeness from search saturation alone.

### Routing policy
Default route: providers ['parallel'], tier default, 8 results per provider.
check_candidates route: ['exa'].
Run baseline discovery on Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results. Use Exa alone for batched check_candidates, explicitly requesting both eligibility tests and identity-matched evidence. Once baseline frontiers are sampled, allow one Exa discovery probe on the weaker frontier if affordable; retain it for further discovery only if it adds useful candidates or unique evidence. Compare marginal outcomes, recognizing provider attribution is overlapping and the initial yield sample is small. Use Parallel for cheap exact-name follow-ups and Exa for consequential unresolved checks; do not repeat settled checks. Budget every variant separately and never trigger broad auto-routing. Exact checks may use 4 results; discovery remains at 8. Apply authoritative-domain filters to evidence checks, not the entire discovery frontier. Use date filters only when logically appropriate, not as a substitute for checking event or effective dates.

### Fetch policy
Fetch only when summaries leave material eligibility or identity uncertain, or when a discovered list offers several new candidates. Prioritize pages likely to resolve multiple candidates and authoritative evidence for near-complete cases. Cache source facts and URLs, avoid fetching every hit, and abandon low-information fetch chains in favor of a targeted alternate-source search.

Make the candidates differ from each other in a meaningful way. Call propose when done.

lessons.title: Verification batches must be budgeted per candidate, not per tool call
lessons.body: In a5fb1e8aae, a six-candidate Exa check cost 0.042 of a 0.080 initial budget; in 62f1804b27, four candidates cost 0.028. Batching did not eliminate per-candidate provider charges. Both achieved full train recall, so these traces establish a cost concentration, not demonstrated recall loss. Estimate the whole batch before dispatch, reuse established predicate evidence, and test cheap first-pass checks or shared-source resolution before paying for speculative expensive checks. Aggregate attribution favors Parallel (78 correct/dollar versus Exa 46.5), but overlaps and differing tasks prevent a causal provider-quality conclusion.

failure_links.why: Despite full train recall, the trace repeatedly rephrased conjunction searches and guessed familiar candidates instead of enforcing the two-no-new-candidate pivot and explicit frontier coverage.
Full train recall does not erase the repeated conjunction-query pattern: numerous similar variants continued after initial checking rather than documenting new partition coverage.

candidates.rationale: Evidence-gated verification cascade: preserve v002's adaptive dual frontiers, but buy broader exploration by replacing routine Exa checks with cheap first-pass checks and selective escalation. Unlike discarded v001, this does not commit to a census anchor.
candidates.instructions: Define X and Y exactly, with entity unit, exclusions, dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search, and one conjunction search. Maintain two deduplicated frontiers and a ledger containing canonical identity, aliases, source-backed X/Y status, unresolved facts and next action. After this baseline, run short discovery/check rounds. First check source-backed candidates on Parallel, supplying existing evidence and requesting identity-matched proof for both predicates, focusing retrieval on the missing fact. Do not recheck already established facts. Treat no result as unresolved, not false; reject only on explicit contradiction or a demonstrably exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising unresolved cases to Exa when identity ambiguity, conflicting sources or inaccessible evidence makes the cheap check insufficient. Rank work by expected verified additions per total remaining resolution cost, but include one neglected subtype or reverse-frontier probe per discovery round to avoid starving unfamiliar candidates. After two discovery searches yield no new plausible identities, prohibit further synonymous conjunction queries until a genuinely different source, partition or frontier has been tried. Track marginal yield and spend by action, including every candidate in a batch. Reserve at least 35% of initial budget for evidence work; halt discovery whenever the estimated pending-check cost needs the remaining funds. Finish with an identity, scope and date audit and submit only supported intersections, without claiming completeness from saturation.
candidates.routing_rules: Use Parallel alone for baseline discovery and first-pass check_candidates, default tier, 8 discovery results and 4 exact-check results. Escalate check_candidates selectively to Exa alone, normally 4 results; never rerun an entire batch because one identity is unresolved. Cost a batch as the sum of candidate queries and provider charges; lower result counts are not assumed cheaper. Permit at most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, retained only for useful new candidates or evidence. Provider yield supports this as a cost hypothesis, not a guarantee of equal accuracy. No broad auto-routing or routine also variants. Apply authoritative-domain filters only to targeted evidence retrieval and relax them when needed. Publication-date filters only when publication dates define eligibility; verify effective dates from content.
candidates.fetch_policy: Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages when they can settle a missing predicate or identity more cheaply than another search, and multi-candidate lists when they add plausible identities. Do not fetch every result or duplicate evidence already sufficient for a decision. If a page is blocked or uninformative, make one targeted alternate-source attempt rather than a fetch chain.

candidates.rationale: Source-bundle adaptive search: change the unit of allocation from individual names to evidence-rich source sections. Keep both frontiers and Exa verification, but amortize discovery and proof across multiple entities without repeating v001's unconditional census commitment.
candidates.instructions: Translate both predicates into exact tests, including entity unit, time boundaries, exclusions and membership rules. Sample X, Y and their conjunction sequentially with one search each. Maintain both candidate frontiers plus a source-section queue: each section records its predicate, scope, pagination, unseen candidates, available facts and extraction/check cost. Prefer sources that explicitly establish one predicate for several identities and offer discriminating fields for checking the other. Run a small pilot on the most promising section: extract canonical identities and aliases, preserve row-level evidence, and check the missing predicate for a small batch before expanding the section. Choose the next section or frontier by newly verified identities per total discovery, extraction and verification spend, not apparent roster size. Never require a complete census before checking; abandon low-yield sections after a pilot and retain unresolved identities for later. Use source subtypes, date ranges, geography or categories to uncover unseen sections, with a reverse-frontier gap check after each productive section. Include unusual eligible subtypes; source descriptions are ranking signals, not grounds for exclusion. Shared evidence can establish X or Y for multiple candidates, but identity and both predicates must be evidenced individually. Resolve aliases, group membership and namesakes explicitly. After two searches produce no new plausible identities, switch source family or frontier instead of rephrasing. Reserve at least 35% of initial budget for checking and resolution, estimate each pending batch's full cost, and stop source expansion when that reserve is needed. Submit evidenced deduplicated intersections; report unresolved scope rather than asserting exhaustive coverage.
candidates.routing_rules: Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for discovery of source sections and targeted alternate sources. Use 4 results for exact-identity follow-ups. Exa alone for small check_candidates batches whose candidates have source-backed anchor evidence; supply that evidence and the exact missing predicate while requiring the final decision to satisfy both tests. Do not pay for a new check when a retrieved source already explicitly settles both conditions and identity. Pilot only as many candidates as can be resolved within the reserve, accounting for per-candidate billing. Allow one Exa source-discovery probe when distinct Parallel source searches stagnate; expand only if marginal yield justifies its higher cost. No auto-routing, routine multi-provider fan-out or broad simultaneous query variants. Restrict domains for source-specific evidence checks, not general discovery. Use publication filters only for logically applicable publication constraints, never as proxies for effective dates.
candidates.fetch_policy: Prioritize a discovered table, directory section or export that supplies evidence for several candidates; confirm scope and pagination before interpreting omissions. Extract candidate identities and useful predicate facts immediately rather than fetching a list and continuing generic conjunction searches. Fetch the next section only after the pilot demonstrates useful yield. Cache row-level provenance and fetch individual authoritative records only for unresolved identities, eligibility or dates. A partial or truncated roster cannot justify rejection or completeness.
